lead.headline: Crew-13 reaches space station in under eight hours after Cape launch
lead.dek: Four astronauts dock seven hours, 55 minutes after an 11:10 a.m. liftoff, the quickest SpaceX crew flight yet
body: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying four astronauts lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 11:10 a.m. ET Thursday, and their Dragon capsule docked at the International Space Station at 7:05 p.m., seven hours and 55 minutes later, the fastest crewed trip the company has flown, NASA and The Associated Press said.

Commander Jessica Watkins, a NASA astronaut who last flew in 2022, is the first Black woman to command a mission to orbit, the AP reported. Her crewmates, NASA pilot Luke Delaney, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov, are first-time fliers. The launch had slipped three weeks because of a fuel system leak.

The crew joins seven people already aboard for a six-month stay. The four Crew-12 members they relieve are to undock Oct. 5 and splash down off Southern California on Oct. 6, CBS News reported, and a cargo Dragon due Oct. 13 carries the final pair of roll-out solar arrays in a station power upgrade begun in 2021.

briefs.headline: Trump backs Paxton, touts truck tariffs at Texas Peterbilt plant
briefs.summary: Trump endorsed Ken Paxton for Senate and credited his truck tariffs with 1,000 PACCAR hires Thursday at Peterbilt's plant in Denton, Texas. The RNC plans 30 Trump rallies through Election Day, CBS Texas reported.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court to review no-bond detention of immigrants
briefs.summary: The justices said Thursday they will hear the administration's appeal defending its policy of jailing immigrants who entered illegally without bond hearings. Most lower courts rejected it; a ruling is expected by June.

briefs.headline: Jobless claims fall to 197,000, near 57-year lows
briefs.summary: Initial claims slipped by 1,000 to 197,000 in the week ended Sept. 26, the Labor Department said Thursday, and Challenger counted 43,281 announced layoffs in September. The September jobs report is due at 8:30 a.m. Friday.
briefs.source: Reuters via The Globe and Mail

briefs.headline: Kansas governor declares disaster as Polo remnants flood state
briefs.summary: Gov. Laura Kelly declared a disaster emergency Wednesday as remnants of Hurricane Polo brought flooding and at least 15 tornadoes to central Kansas, KWCH reported. Dodge City was under a flash flood emergency Thursday.

briefs.headline: US sends third aircraft carrier toward Iran, official says
briefs.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt group left San Diego on Sunday and a Marine force with more than 2,000 Marines followed a day later, a U.S. official told Al Jazeera. Three carriers will be in place by late November.

briefs.headline: France shuts 400 schools as student protests reach 2,000 arrests
briefs.summary: Education Minister Edouard Geffray said late Thursday more than 400 schools would stay closed Friday; police have made about 2,000 arrests and 40 principals are among the injured.

briefs.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever ties as Tigray fighting intensifies
briefs.summary: Ethiopia closed its Asmara embassy and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats Thursday, accusing Eritrea of hostility; Asmara said it would cut all ties in kind. Addis Ababa also expelled an Egyptian diplomat.

briefs.headline: Brazil opens probe into alleged US plan to fund far-right groups
briefs.summary: Attorney General Jorge Messias sought the inquiry after a Guardian report alleged a $1 million U.S. plan to fund groups opposing Brazil's Supreme Court. Brazil votes Sunday, with Lula facing Flavio Bolsonaro.

briefs.headline: Deputies kill Moundsville man after couple shot dead
briefs.summary: Marshall County deputies shot Cyle Fabrizio, 25, early Thursday as he held a gun to a girl's head; her parents, David and Monica Will, lay dead inside.

briefs.headline: State drug czar Loyd resigns after two years
briefs.summary: Dr. Stephen Loyd confirmed Tuesday he has left the Office of Drug Control Policy, saying he never spoke with Gov. Morrisey beyond one text message.

briefs.headline: Appalachian Power files Black Diamond status report
briefs.summary: Appalachian Power told the PSC Thursday it is still doing due diligence on buying Black Diamond Power, which serves Wyoming, Raleigh and Clay counties.

briefs.headline: State collects $570M in September, $16M over estimate
briefs.summary: General revenue ran almost $16 million above estimate last month and $1.41 billion for the year to date, Revenue Secretary Eric Nelson said Thursday.

regional.item: A judge denied bond Thursday for Joshua Deel of Lesage, charged with the July 21 stabbing deaths of his ex-wife and her two teenagers.
Content creator Michael Bowman, 35, of Charlotte is charged with strangulation over an Aug. 28 incident on Spring Street in St. Albans.
Sheriff Rick Woodyard asked Wood County commissioners Thursday to start buying a new armored response vehicle, about $370,000.
Two Hinton officials are taking a nine-week ARC grants course that makes the city eligible for a $50,000 capacity-building application.

away.item: Bennington police are investigating after a pedestrian was struck in an Elm Street crosswalk Wednesday and taken to Albany Medical Center.

hotspots.item: The county visitors bureau approved a $52,300 budget for 2026-27 at its Sept. 22 meeting, 41% of it for marketing, the Echo reported Tuesday.
Surf City posted notice Thursday of a special meeting Tuesday, Oct. 6, at 5 p.m. in its council chambers, citing G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5).

briefs.headline: Valleyview parents push for school bus on East Austin Road
briefs.summary: Residents want the Route 97 school special extended into Valleyview after BC Transit denied a stop; they say children walk a narrow dip in the dark.

briefs.headline: Harry Loder Park parking options go to council's last meeting
briefs.summary: A staff report Monday offers 10 more stalls for about $15,000 or 24 with lighting for about $90,000; Northern Health favours the larger plan but has no funding for it.

briefs.headline: Tsawwassen First Nation names two elders killed in Delta crash
briefs.summary: The nation identified wilapiya (Barb Joe) and Virginia Splockton. Delta police say two others remain critical, the driver has been released and nothing suggests the crash was intentional.

briefs.headline: Ipsos poll puts B.C. Conservatives two points ahead of NDP
briefs.summary: The Sept. 25-29 survey of 1,001 adults has the Conservatives at 42%, up seven in two weeks, and the NDP at 40, down five; half disapprove of the early election call.

briefs.headline: Carney names Pacific Link pipeline first national-interest project
briefs.summary: Carney announced the designation Thursday in Fort McMurray. The 1,200-kilometre line from Bruderheim, Alta., to Roberts Bank near Delta, B.C., is estimated at $35.2 billion to $43.7 billion; conditions are due by Sept. 1, 2027.

briefs.headline: Budget watchdog puts Alto high-speed rail at $75B to $113B
briefs.summary: The Parliamentary Budget Officer's report Thursday on the Toronto-Quebec City corridor, excluding a Kingston stop, runs above official estimates of $60 billion to $90 billion.

briefs.headline: DeepMind watermark tags AI-designed proteins
briefs.summary: Google DeepMind's SynthIDBio hid signatures in protein sequences and 3D structures; its detector found all watermarked sequences and 99.8% of structures in a Nature paper published Wednesday, with binding unchanged.

briefs.headline: Urine RNA test detects 95% of localized bladder cancers
briefs.summary: A Stanford Medicine test reading tumor RNA shed into urine identified 95% of localized bladder cancers and cleared 90% of people without cancer across 683 samples, beating cytology. It appears Friday in Nature Medicine.

briefs.headline: Europe logs record 41 days of strong heat stress, Copernicus says
briefs.summary: About 80% of Europe saw strong heat stress, above 90F feels-like, for a record 41 days this summer and 52% saw very strong stress above 100F, the EU's Copernicus monitor said Friday. Western Europe had its hottest summer on record.

briefs.headline: MIND diet adherence linked to slower brain tissue loss
briefs.summary: Among 1,647 Framingham Heart Study adults scanned over 12 years, each 3-point rise in MIND diet score was tied to 20% less grey matter loss, about 2.5 years of delayed brain aging, in an observational study in JNNP.

briefs.headline: Hawley, Murphy bill would make AI firms liable for agent attacks
briefs.summary: Sens. Josh Hawley and Chris Murphy introduced the AI Agent Accountability Act, which would make developers and operators civilly and criminally liable for hacking by AI agents, after a Wednesday Senate Homeland Security panel hearing.

briefs.headline: OpenAI parts ways with three safety researchers over leak
briefs.summary: OpenAI said it "parted ways with three individuals" for violating its policies on handling sensitive information. The Wall Street Journal reported they shared confidential material with an outside AI safety group; none were named.

briefs.headline: Independent tests put Gemini 4 Argon level with rivals
briefs.summary: Artificial Analysis scored Google's Gemini 4 Argon 53 on its Intelligence Index, level with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and below Claude Opus 5.5 at 58; Vals AI ranked it first on its index at 68.9%.

weather_ear: Friday's forecast arrives from the weather desk at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster ran no regional line; the September jobs report is due at 8:30, Brazil votes Sunday, and the Division Series open Saturday.
